title: Netweb Technologies India Ltd - 543945 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Netweb Q1 FY27 revenue rose 172.1% YoY to INR8,197 million with PAT of INR853 million (10.3% margin), driven by the AI segment at 62% of revenue.
summary.overview: Netweb reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and profit, with revenue from operations of INR8,197 million (+172.1% YoY) and PAT of INR853 million (+179.9% YoY). Operating EBITDA was INR1,205 million at a 14.7% margin. The AI segment contributed INR5,106 million (62% of revenue, +484% YoY), while HPC and Private Cloud contributed INR1,253 million and INR1,353 million. Working capital moved up: inventory days rose from 86 to 110 as the company built raw-material stock against memory and component shortages, while receivable days fell from 86 to 78; net debt was INR1,999 million.

segments.name: AI systems
segments.commentary: INR5,105.7 million, 62% of Q1 revenue, growing 484% YoY; management expects AI to be roughly 40-45% of the order book.

segments.name: HPC
segments.commentary: INR1,252.94 million in Q1; management says the three pillars (AI, HPC, Private Cloud) are all growing and intact.

segments.name: Private Cloud / HCI
segments.commentary: INR1,353.46 million in Q1; Tyrone Skylus indigenous private cloud platform targets data localisation and sovereignty needs.

guidance_outlook: Order book INR25,069 million as of 30 June 2026, plus L1 of INR8,480 million; management cites about INR3,400 crore combined and a pipeline of about INR104,100 million (INR10,401 crore) that now includes strategic orders.
Management guides about 60% pipeline conversion over 18-24 months; the earlier 18-month timeline now stretches to 18-24 months.
Execution cycle now guided at 16-20 weeks versus 8-12 weeks earlier, and may stretch or come early.
Margins guided at 13-14%; management says Q1's 14.7% EBITDA margin is within this range and will remain similar.
Management said it does not see memory prices softening for the next couple of quarters, perhaps a year.
Management says the order book and pipeline support about two years of revenue; a call on how the year splits by half was deferred.
risks_watch: Working capital: inventory days rose to 110, and management said the company will need working capital for growth. Management did not rule out capital raising (debt or equity), and the enabling resolution is valid for 12 months.
Component and memory price inflation and scarcity; management says it expects no softening in memory prices for a couple of quarters or perhaps a year.
Strategic and bulky orders are not separately reported going forward, and comparable prior-quarter pipeline figures were not provided.
Pipeline composition by segment was not disclosed, and conversion (about 60% over 18-24 months) is not quantified per year.
Prior-period balance sheet restated for a shift in inventory valuation to moving weighted average cost from FIFO (described as P4 in transcript).
Research and development spending is expensed, not capitalised, and its size is not quantified; the physical AI and quantum programs have no revenue guidance.
Confident and promotional on demand and margins; evasive on pipeline breakdown, capital raise intent, R&D quantum and revenue timing for new verticals.
Our revenue from operations for the quarter stood at INR8,197 million, reflecting a strong year-on-year growth of 172.1%.
We do not want a situation where a very large growth looking at the pipeline is available for us to grab and we don't grab it because of the lack of capital.
So there is no strategic order now. All orders are normal orders actually. The strategic is the new normal.

financial_highlights.metric: Return on capital employed / Return on equity

financial_highlights.change: Inventory days 86 to 110 (Mar to Jun 2026); receivable days 86 to 78

qa_highlights.question: Mix of AI orders, average ticket size, and customer application types in the order book.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave order book plus L1 at about INR3,400 crore and said AI should be about 40-45% of the order book; it did not disclose ticket size or application-level detail.

qa_highlights.question: Whether incremental capacity or assembly facilities are needed to support 50-60% growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing facilities were built for INR3,000-plus crore turnover; no major capex needed, only light and routine capex, and no new capex guided.

qa_highlights.question: Comparable prior-quarter pipeline, L1 and order book including strategic orders.
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the prior-quarter figures at hand; said the pipeline has grown but did not give the number, and strategic orders are no longer reported separately.

qa_highlights.question: Why margins rose despite memory price inflation; whether inventory build enabled higher pricing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are within the 13-14% range, pricing power and direct technology-provider relationships protect margins, and it denied overcharging customers.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the INR1,200 crore QIP reported in the press.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had not raised any money; an enabling resolution valid for 12 months was passed for growth capital, mainly working capital, with no M&A.

qa_highlights.question: Restatement of prior-period balance sheet and conversion timeline of the pipeline by FY27 and FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: Restatement is from shifting inventory valuation from FIFO to moving weighted average cost; management would not split the pipeline conversion between FY27 and FY28, reiterating 60% over 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue R&D spend and expected revenue from physical AI and quantum computing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no revenue guidance or R&D quantum for physical AI and quantum; said R&D team is about 125 people and results would show in coming quarters.

capex_capacity: Management said the facilities were built to sustain turnover of INR3,000-plus crore and does not see a need for major capex at current levels; only light and routine capex continues, with no new capex guided.
Company describes itself as capability-driven rather than capacity-driven, with no contract manufacturing; it manufactures in-house.

Company will need working capital for growth; enabling resolution for capital raise (debt or equity) valid for 12 months, stated to be for working capital only, with no M&A; no capital raise has been executed.
Inventory days rose from 86 in March to 110 in June 2026 due to deliberate raw-material buildup to secure key inputs amid AI compute demand and component shortages.
Execution cycle now 16-20 weeks versus 8-12 weeks earlier, which management said can stretch or come early.
R&D team of about 125 people; R&D is expensed, not capitalised, and management did not quantify R&D spend.
demand_pricing: Order book INR25,069.35 million as of 30 June 2026 plus L1 of INR8,480.47 million; management put the combined figure at about INR3,400 crore.
Pipeline stated at INR104,100 million (INR10,401 crore), now including strategic orders; prior pipeline excluding strategic orders was INR4,400 crore per management.
Order book mix guided at about 40-45% AI, with the balance across HPC and Private Cloud; management says all three pillars are growing.
Management expects about 60% pipeline conversion over 18-24 months (earlier 18 months), and said the order book and pipeline support about two years of revenue.
Around INR430 crore of the INR1,600 crore strategic order (cited from the May call) was executed in the June quarter.
Margin guidance 13-14%; Q1 EBITDA margin of 14.7% described as within range; management said memory prices are not expected to soften for a couple of quarters, maybe a year.
Management said pricing power and existing order contracts protect margins, with new orders priced on current component costs; existing orders not repriced.
Management said exports are 4-5% of book and the company is not focusing on exports; domestic demand (India AI Mission, sovereign AI, CSPs, on-prem government) is the focus.

So basically, 8 to 12 weeks was earlier. Now we are mentioning basically 16 to 20 weeks.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand, pricing power and margin stability, but evasive on pipeline breakdown, the enabling capital resolution, R&D spend and revenue timing for physical AI and quantum.

growth.why: Q1 revenue rose 172.1% YoY to INR8,197m and the order book plus L1 (~INR3,400 crore) supports about two years of revenue, but management guides no new capex, says existing facilities were built for INR3,000-plus crore turnover, and gives no explicit revenue growth guidance.
